newsitem.title: UK: M&S sees "substantial impact" of store buys.
newsitem.headline: M&S sees "substantial impact" of store buys.

text.p: British food and clothing retailer Marks and Spencer Plc expects to see a "substantial impact" in the next financial year from the addition of 19 stores which it has agreed to buy from Littlewoods for 192.5 million stg, deputy chairman Keith Oates said.
"The impact will be in the next financial year but it will be a substantial impact," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television broadcast on Friday.
Marks and Spencer announced it had bought the stores at its annual meeting on Thursday and chairman Sir Richard Greenbury said it would enhance shareholder value.

Oates said the deal would add over 600,000 square feet to sales space and added that although sales per square foot might not reach the company's average of 600 stg, they should be "a lot more than the 200 stg or so that Littlewood's traded at."
Oates said on food sales, "we will get back into not only reasonable volumes but also a much greater sales performance" in the next few months.
He said gross margins, which have always been "good," should be steady.
"We don't anticipate them rising but on the other hand we do see that we can maintain them," Oates said.
